items.titleEn: Barrick beats Q3 earnings expectations as gold production improves, maintains 2026 guidance
items.summaryEn: Correction: This article has been updated to correct the third-quarter earnings comparison. An earlier version incorrectly stated that the company missed earnings expectations because of incomplete estimates. (Kitco News) - Barrick Mining Corporation (NYSE: B, TSX: ABX) reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings as stronger gold production and higher realized prices helped offset rising operating costs. The mining giant also maintained its full-year production guidance as operational improvements continued across its portfolio. The senior miner reported adjusted net earnings of $1.35 billion, or $0.82 per share, for the third quarter, up 41% from $0.58 per share reported during the same period last year. The results beat consensus estimates, as analysts had expected earnings of $0.79 per share.

Gold and silver prices extend post-election rebound, central banks on pace to beat 2025 purchases – Heraeus
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold and silver are continuing to build on last week’s strong rally following the Democratic sweep of the midterm elections, but the precious metals will likely face pressure from resurgent oil prices and elevated Fed rate expectations, according to analysts at Heraeus. In their latest update, the analysts noted that gold prices saw a sharp rebound last week soon after dropping to a fresh 2026 low. “Having fallen by more than 15% from its late-August high, the price briefly dropped below $3,900/oz, breaking the June low near $3,950/oz,” they wrote. “The Democrats’ sweep of both houses of Congress then triggered gold’s largest daily gain since August, and the price recovered above $4,000/oz.”
